fields.accroche: This site, from methodology to code: PRD, art direction, design system, mockups, and finally implementation in Vue.

capture.alt: Portfolio homepage: the name, the tagline, and animated contour lines in the background.

contexte.html:
As an engineering student at ESIEA, I am looking for a final-year internship in full-stack development.

Until now, I have presented myself using a CV, LinkedIn, and GitHub. While these resources list my skills, they fail to showcase my methodology, my creativity, or who I am—leaving recruiters with no real way to get a sense of my unique identity.

besoin.html:
A single platform that showcases the rigor of an engineer, the creativity of a web developer, and my own personality.

Two types of readers to cater to. The HR recruiter—who screens quickly and lacks a technical background—needs to grasp my profile and be able to download my CV in one click. The tech lead, meanwhile, wants to read a case study, understand the rationale behind my choices, and access the code.

description.html: On my personal server (Proxmox), inside a Docker container, behind Nginx Proxy Manager.
WCAG 2.2 Level AA; all animations respect the "reduce motion" setting.
My availability changes from one week to the next: the work is broken down into small, deliverable stages.

fields.methode_intro: Seven phases, in sequence, each with its own deliverable, Git branch, and validation step before moving on to the next.

description.html: Generic components, “bricks”, all built on tokens: no hard value. Each has its own page in a development catalog, with its live settings, states and “reduced movement” mode.

choix.compromis: More time before the first screen, fewer revisions afterward.

choix.titre: The background is animated using native WebGL.

description.html: The contour lines on the landing page are based on a component originally written for a 3D library, now rewritten in WebGL 2 without that dependency—one less dependency to manage. It is a static image with subtle motion, which pauses when moved off-screen.
Fonts served by the site, a Docker container on my own server, audience measurement using my own tool—Dashility: no third-party services, no consent banner.

choix.titre: Vue 3, Vite, and TypeScript, without Nuxt

description.html: Each page is pre-rendered as full HTML using vite-ssg, for SEO purposes. Bilingual routing, head tags, and the sitemap are assembled by hand, in small, readable segments.

choix.compromis: more custom code than with Nuxt.

resultats.libelle: stages, from PRD to code, with each one validated before the next
generic components, each in the catalog
written decisions, each with its reasoning
section funds, as opposed to just one in the first artistic direction

conclusion.html: Lighthouse: 100 in performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO.

description.html: Making a decision when presented with two to six displayed versions is faster than debating over a document.
An automated design assistant was tested twice and subsequently removed: it imposed its own workflow on a project that already had one of its own.
One line and one reason per decision: a choice, once made, is not revisited.
